attributes.name: Upper etched unit
attributes.Unit_Description: Indurated, rugged, moderately-to-heavily cratered, light-to-intermediate toned unit located along and on the northern Jezero crater rim and wall, along the interior margin of Jezero crater, and throughout Nili Planum. Overlies units Nnp1 and cr in Nili Planum and conformably overlies unit Nle in Jezero crater. Contains three different surface expressions with varying morphologic and erosional textures that grade into one another without clear or systematic stratigraphic contacts: a ridged expression in northern Jezero and northeastern Nili Planum, a heavily cratered expression in northern Nili Planum, and a light-toned rugged expression in southern Nili Planum (Figure 3). Type area: lat 18.67°N, long 77.57°E and lat 18.68°N, long 76.86°E and lat 17.77°N, long 76.86°E respectively.
attributes.Additional_Characteristics: Occurs at elevations ranging from -2707 m within Jezero to -1787 m in Nili Planum. Ridged expression has ridges trending northeast to southwest, and overlies the Jezero crater rim (18.56°N, 77.28°E). Heavily cratered expression has a rougher, heavily cratered surface with no preferential direction indicated by erosional textures. Light-toned rugged expression has a moderately rough, cratered surface with variegated tones and very sharply defined ridged margins that often forms linear outcrops extending up to 5 kilometers in length (17.78°N, 77.31°E) and can be associated with raised linear ridges in unit Nnp1 (for example, 18.19°N, 77.06°E; 17.86°N, 77.03°E). Associated with olivine and variable carbonate (Goudge and others, 2015; Bramble and others, 2017). Previously mapped as the 'fractured unit' by Bramble and others (2017), and inside Jezero crater as the 'mottled terrain' by Goudge and others (2015).
attributes.Unit_Interpretation: Volcanic ash deposit that drapes underlying units Nnp1, cr, and Nle. Could also be other clastic deposit of volcanic or eolian origin. The three distinct surface expressions could result from differential erosion or cementation, as no clear or systematic stratigraphic contacts are discernable between the three surface expressions. Ridges in the ridged Nue unit are yardangs (Day and Dorn, 2019). Long linear occurrences of the light-toned rugged Nue unit could have formed through infilling of preexisting fractures created by the Isidis impact.

attributes.name: Eolian bedform unit
attributes.Unit_Description: Light-toned, linear, commonly parallel low-relief ridges prevalent in local topographic lows such as impact craters, including along the interior margin of Jezero crater, and at the base of steep scarps throughout Nili Planum. Superposes other map units. Type area: lat 18.41°N, long 77.36°E
attributes.Additional_Characteristics: Low-relief ridges are up to several hundred meters in length and spacing is on the order of 10s of meters. Bifurcations and overlapping ridges are common. Crestlines trend approximately N-S, but can vary locally. Low-relief ridges occur in fields up to several km2 in area.
attributes.Unit_Interpretation: Amazonian-aged bedforms and transverse aeolian ridges (TARs) composed of unconsolidated sediment oriented orthogonal to the dominant east-west wind direction (Day and Dorn, 2019).

attributes.name: Smooth unit, undivided
attributes.Unit_Description: Smooth, intermediate-toned, commonly featureless unit with rare dark-toned occurrences (for example, 17.85°N, 77.50°E) that occurs predominantly on the steep interior slopes of Jezero crater and Sedona crater, on Nili Planum east of Sedona crater, and in local depressions. Type area: lat 17.84°N, long 77.68°E
attributes.Unit_Interpretation: Sediments contributed from mass wasting, a widespread deposit of volcanic, or eolian origin, or residual accumulation of sand, pebbles, and cobbles due to deflation of the landscape.

attributes.name: Nili Planum 2 unit
attributes.Unit_Description: Rugged, heavily cratered, light- to intermediate-toned, planar unit, margins defined by low-relief, sharp, lobate scarps, located throughout Nili Planum and on the western rim of Jezero crater (lat 18.39°N, long 77.28°E). Erosional texture contains meter-scale blocks at HiRISE-scale. Caps lobate mesa sequences by overlying units Nue, Nnp1, or cr. Banding or stratification visible along some margins (for example, 17.87°N, 77.09°E). Type areas at different elevations: 18.19°N, long 77.01°E; 18.39°N, 77.27°E; 18.08°N, 77.26°E
attributes.Additional_Characteristics: Outcrops as small as 0.02 km2 or as large as 23 km2 and span 241 m of elevation range (-2067 to -1826 m elevation) within the map area. Associated with mafic composition (Bramble and others, 2017). Previously mapped as the 'thin capping unit' by Goudge and others (2015) and as the 'capping unit' by Bramble and others (2017).
attributes.Unit_Interpretation: Volcanic ash or eolian airfall deposit emplaced during the Late Noachian, possibly in multiple, localized episodes of deposition, that drapes underlying topography, for example on the Jezero crater rim. Correlates with unit Njf based on common stratigraphic position and shared textural and morphologic characteristics.
